THIS IS THE PACKET'S SHARPEST LIVE CONTRADICTION AND I AM SETTLING IT AGAINST THE OTHER SIDE. combat-core/v0717-stance-table (UPHELD, 1 critic) states 'At mastery 9 the damage row is 0.86/1.18/1.4, i.e. the wiki's 0.9/1.2/1.4 rounded, which CONFIRMS the ledger's mastery-9 reading rather than overturning it.' new_findings.text: A live finding-vs-finding contradiction that no single-claim lens could see, settled here from the artifact. combat-core/v0717-stance-table (UPHELD) closes with 'At mastery 9 the damage row is 0.86/1.18/1.4, i.e. the wiki's 0.9/1.2/1.4 rounded, which CONFIRMS the ledger's mastery-9 reading rather than overturning it.' Five other UPHELD findings say the opposite. Both cannot be true, and the deciding artifact is skilldata.xml: skill 1000 (stance mastery) spans lines 10-79 with exactly ten <level> blocks, and the tenth block is ':74 <value>10</value>' paired with ':75 <required>9</required>'. The scale is the <value> column, which runs 1..10; <required> is the skill-point prerequisite and runs 1..9. So 'mastery-9' is a misread of the prerequisite column, and the web multipliers §1t99s0§.as:3262 (0.5+0.04m) and :3265 (1+0.02m) hit the ledger's 0.9 and 1.2 EXACTLY at m=10 while missing them at m=9 (0.86, 1.18). An exact hit beats a rounded one. The reconciliation clause in combat-core/v0717-stance-table must be struck before the rewrite absorbs it, or a writer picking between two surviving findings inherits a coin flip. Note the rest of that finding (the complete v0.717 stance table, Heavy defence x0.8) is unaffected — only its mastery-9 reconciliation falls.

new_findings.text: The reason s26c/the-271-cap-IS-the-shipped-level-80-base-stat-cap and progression/271-cap-explained disagree is a single comparison operator, and it is on the page. §1t5957s0§.as:3344 gates the ATK add-button on 'stat < 1 + (_loc2_ + 10) * 3' — a STRICT less-than — and :3422 grants exactly +3. Base ATK is 1 (§1t1523s0§.as:2567 sets §1t9408s0§ to 1 on stat reset; :3457 audits spend as (ATK - 1) / 3, which independently pins base 1 step 3). The reachable set is therefore {1, 4, 7, ..., 268, 271}, and 271 = 1 + 3*90 is ON the lattice: at 268 the gate is still open, the grant fires, ATK becomes 271, and only then does the button hide. 'Unreachable because the panel stops granting' inverts what the operator does — a strict '<' hides the button AFTER the cap is reached, not before. The budget half is not close either: §1t1523s0§.as:2577 sets the pool to (getLevel() - 1) * 3 = 237 at the level cap of 80 (:362 'public static const §1t9470s0§:int = 80;'), against a 90-point cost. Bank the operator, not just the formula: a rebuild that ships '<=' produces a 274 cap.
new_findings.lane_impact: L4 progression: ship STAT_CAP_{ATK,DEF,SPD} = 1 + (level+10)*3 with a STRICT '<' grant gate, base 1 step 3, budget (level-1)*3. Strike the 'unreachable in one stat' clause from s26c/the-271-cap-IS-the-shipped-level-80-base-stat-cap.

new_findings.text: Every reach finding in the corpus reaches for android InputManager.as to establish that slashLength is a stroke LENGTH BUDGET rather than a hitbox radius, and carries a C2 hedge for doing so. It does not have to. The web v0.717 payload ships the same class and the obfuscator left the field name intact: §1t1541s0§.as:106-108 'public static function §1t10094s0§(param1:int) : * { maxDistance = param1; }', and §1t99s0§.as:3158 pushes the just-computed per-stance reach into it — the exact twin of android MCSPlayer.as:3094 'InputManager.setMaxDistance(this.slashLength)'. So the whole chain SPD -> baseSlashLength -> per-stance slashLength -> InputManager.maxDistance is web-side end to end, and the units question ('is this stage px?') is answered in the target build rather than inferred across a build boundary. Nobody has recorded this: grepping the corpus for the reach chain returns android InputManager cites only.
new_findings.lane_impact: L5 combat-core: drop the android C2 hedge from every reach finding — cite §1t1541s0§.as:106-108 instead of android InputManager.as:106-109.

new_findings.text: Unclaimed, and it changes the reach model's shape. §1t99s0§.as:219-224 is a third branch of the same buff switch that grants minDamage x1.5 (:213) and defense x1.5 (:217): 'else if(§1t1523s0§.§1t9725s0§(§1t1523s0§.§1t9463s0§)) { this.minDamage *= 0.5; this.defense *= 0.5; this.§1t4420s0§ *= 0.5; }'. §1t4420s0§ is baseSlashLength, so a live debuff HALVES reach at the base, before the stance multiplier and before the Heavy floor of 100 — meaning under this state Light runs 84-147 px and Heavy is pinned at its 100 floor for every speed value. The constants: §1t1523s0§.as:328/330/332 give buff ids 1 (ATK), 2 (DEF), 3 (SPD), and :348 'internal static const §1t9463s0§:int = 11;' is the debuff, checked on its OWN timer slot at :5011-5017 ('if(param1 == §1t9463s0§) return §1t7356s0§(§1t9433s0§) > ...') rather than the shared buff slot the other three use — i.e. a curse can run concurrently with a buff. Every reach finding in the corpus models base -> stance -> floor with no debuff term.

new_findings.text: Both banked web-side reinforce findings cite §1t401s0§.as:664-688, which is the DISPLAY block — it selects getString(850)/(851)/(852) by weapon level and prints them. That proves what the menu SAYS, not what the transaction TAKES, and a rebuild written from it ships string ids. The ACTION block is 440 lines further down and is the one to port: §1t401s0§.as:1110-1144 requires and spends stat ids 20064 / 20065 / 20066 on the same <30 / <60 / else key, :1087 charges a flat 'cost = 5000;' debited at :1146, :1106-1108 forces weaponlevel 59 for itemID 13022, and :1147 resets 'weapon.uses = 0;'. Recording the distinction because a citation audit that treats :664-688 and :1110-1147 as the same fact will not notice that only one of them carries the item IDs. Names still resolve through android-sourced data (itemdata.xml:10420/10429/10438 -> strings.json['4241']/['4242']/['4243'] = Silver Ore / Titanium Ore / Uncut Diamond), so the C2 hedge is discharged for the mechanic and the ids, NOT for the display names.

new_findings.text: An independent arithmetic corroboration of the 6x6 rule that costs nothing and closes a loop between two findings banked from unrelated artifacts. I counted the territory bitmap myself: reference/extracted/android/110_Mobile_MapBitmapData.bin decodes as a 63x72 GIF in palette mode with exactly 735 lit pixels (PIL, threshold >127 on the L conversion), one per existing territory — matching the banked world-map finding. The war/room finding in this packet establishes that every territory subdivides into exactly 6x6 = 36 node ids (WarHexUI.as:195-197 x6 on both axes, walked by getShiftedNodeId at :208). 735 x 36 = 26,460, which is precisely the '26,460-sector world' figure a separate upheld finding banked from the node generator. Three artifacts — a GIF, a UI class and a generator — agree to the unit. This is the kind of check a per-claim lens cannot run, and it means the world's node count is a DERIVED quantity a rebuild can assert, not a measured one.
